rv.q: 1984 succeeds in bringing new life to Orwell’s work; I left the Playhouse thoroughly removed from myself.

Headlong’s sharp, atmospheric adaptation of Orwell’s satire on 1948 follows the sequence of the novel and incorporates recognisable portions of Orwell’s text in the dialogue, but makes it seem like a disturbing image of our near future.
This brilliant and stylish adaptation from writer-directors Robert Icke and Duncan Macmillan remains faithful to the classic whilst introducing a clever new twist.

cn.t: Icke and Macmillan's visceral adaptation breathes new life into Orwell's classic with chilling stagecraft and strong performances. Critics praise its stylish, ruthless staging that makes for brilliant, if jolting, theatre.
